finalCtaDescription: Before you proceed, speak with our experts. Revival of Struck off Companies can directly impact bank accounts, property, contracts, tax refunds, GST records, litigation, creditor claims, director status and future business continuity. Do not wait until limitation, bank, tax or property issues become more complicated. A short discussion today can help you understand whether revival is possible, what evidence is required and how to restore the company correctly.

blocks.text: Revival of Struck off Companies is the legal process of restoring a company’s name to the Register of Companies after it has been removed by the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act.

It matters because a struck-off company is treated as dissolved, but its liabilities, obligations and pending responsibilities do not simply disappear. If the company had assets, bank balance, pending contracts, litigation, tax matters, business operations, property, investments, regulatory approvals or stakeholder claims, revival may be required to restore its legal existence.

This service is relevant for directors, shareholders, members, creditors, workmen, investors, lenders, property buyers, tax teams, business families and promoters who need a struck-off company restored for business continuation, asset recovery, compliance filing, litigation, bank operations, statutory closure or transaction completion.
Revival of Struck off Companies is not a licence. It is a statutory restoration process for bringing a struck-off company back to active legal status.
It is regulated by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Registrar of Companies and National Company Law Tribunal under the Companies Act, 2013, NCLT Rules and MCA strike-off framework.

It is not mandatory for every struck-off company. It becomes necessary where the company, member, creditor, workman or aggrieved person needs the company restored for business, compliance, asset, liability, contract, litigation or statutory reasons.
In simple terms…
Revival of Struck off Companies means asking the NCLT to restore a company that ROC has removed from the register.

Once the company is restored, ROC updates the company’s status, and the company is generally placed in a position as if its name had not been struck off, subject to NCLT directions and compliance completion.
From a compliance perspective…

Revival requires checking ROC strike-off reason, STK notice history, STK-7 date, limitation period, company operations, bank records, GST records, income-tax records, invoices, contracts, financial statements, pending AOC-4/MGT-7 filings, director status, outstanding liabilities and evidence that restoration is justified.

From a risk perspective, revival should not be filed only because the company wants to become active again. The petition must show a legally acceptable reason such as continuing business, existing assets, pending liabilities, creditor interest, workman claim, property record, tax matter, litigation, bank account, contractual obligation or “just” grounds for restoration.

faqs.q: What is Revival of Struck off Companies?
faqs.a: Revival of Struck off Companies is the legal process of restoring a company’s name to the Register of Companies after ROC has struck it off.

faqs.q: Is Revival of Struck off Companies a licence?
faqs.a: No. It is not a licence. It is a statutory restoration process under company law.

faqs.q: Which section applies to revival of struck-off company?
faqs.a: Section 252 of the Companies Act, 2013 is the main provision for restoration of a struck-off company.

faqs.q: Which authority handles company revival?
faqs.a: The National Company Law Tribunal handles restoration petitions, and ROC updates the company status after the NCLT order is filed.

faqs.q: Why does ROC strike off a company?
faqs.a: ROC may strike off a company for non-commencement, non-operation, non-filing, non-maintenance of registered office or other statutory grounds under Section 248.

faqs.q: Can a struck-off company be revived?
faqs.a: Yes. A struck-off company can be revived if the applicant shows valid grounds under Section 252 and NCLT is satisfied.

faqs.q: Who can file revival petition?
faqs.a: The company, member, creditor, workman or aggrieved person may apply depending on the route and facts.

faqs.q: What is the time limit for revival?
faqs.a: A Section 252(1) appeal is generally within 3 years from ROC order. Section 252(3) application by company/member/creditor/workman can be made before expiry of 20 years from Gazette publication.

faqs.q: What is STK-7?
faqs.a: STK-7 is the notice of striking off and dissolution published after ROC removes the company’s name from the register.

faqs.q: What is NCLT-9?
faqs.a: NCLT-9 is the form used for appeal or application under Section 252 for restoration of company name.

faqs.q: Is bank balance enough for revival?
faqs.a: Bank balance is helpful evidence, but the petition should also explain why restoration is just and necessary.

faqs.q: Can a company be revived for property transfer?
faqs.a: Yes. If the struck-off company owns property, revival may be required for sale, transfer, mutation or title clearance.

faqs.q: Can a creditor apply for revival?
faqs.a: Yes. A creditor can apply if the company’s restoration is needed for recovery or enforcement of claim.

faqs.q: Can a workman apply for revival?
faqs.a: Yes. A workman can apply where rights or dues are affected by the strike-off.

faqs.q: Can a struck-off company file ROC forms directly?
faqs.a: Generally, restoration is required before regular filings can be completed, subject to MCA/ROC system and NCLT order directions.

faqs.q: What happens after NCLT restoration order?
faqs.a: The certified copy of NCLT order must be filed with ROC, after which ROC restores the company’s name and pending compliances must be completed.

faqs.q: Does revival remove all penalties?
faqs.a: No. Revival restores legal status, but pending filings, additional fees, penalties and compliance defaults may still need to be handled.

faqs.q: Can DIN be activated after company revival?
faqs.a: DIN issues may need separate review. Where DIN was affected due to strike-off/default, post-restoration steps may be required.

faqs.q: Can company be revived only for closure?
faqs.a: Yes. In some cases, the company is revived only to regularise filings, settle assets/liabilities and then complete lawful strike-off or liquidation.

faqs.q: Can fresh company incorporation replace revival?
faqs.a: Fresh incorporation may work only where old company has no assets, liabilities, contracts, bank balance, tax matters or legal need. Otherwise revival may be required.

faqs.q: Is NCLT hearing required?
faqs.a: Yes. NCLT generally hears the applicant and ROC before passing restoration order.

faqs.q: Can ROC object to revival?
faqs.a: Yes. ROC may file observations or objections, especially if filings are pending or grounds for revival are weak.

faqs.q: What documents are required for revival?
faqs.a: COI, MOA/AOA, MCA master data, STK-7, bank statements, tax/GST records, invoices, financials, pending forms list, board resolution, affidavit and evidence of business/assets/liabilities may be required.

faqs.q: What is the biggest mistake in company revival?
faqs.a: The biggest mistake is filing a generic petition without limitation calculation, STK-7 date, evidence matrix, compliance gap report and post-revival filing plan.
